title: Rotor Rescue: Scrapyard Magnet Pick-and-Pay
one_liner: A price-sheet-plus-gauss-meter program that pays scrapyards for magnet-dense motors and rotors they currently sell as steel and copper.
customer: Rare-earth magnet recyclers and magnet makers needing domestic recycled feed (they pay per kg with assay). Scrapyards, motor rebuilders and appliance/HVAC recyclers are the sellers.
problem: The rare-earth bottleneck is 'collection and disassembly rather than recovery chemistry.' Hard-drive magnet removal often costs more than the material is worth. Yards sell EV drive units, servo and elevator motors, and e-bike hub motors by copper and steel weight, and the NdFeB rotors go into the steel shred.
solution: Skip HDDs and target a short list of heavy, magnet-dense items. Yards get a phone app plus a $150 gauss meter that identifies magnet-bearing units and shows a payout per unit or per rotor. A mobile pull cell or the yard's own labor removes rotors. We aggregate and assay them, then sell a certified, traceable magnet-feed stream to recyclers.
why_now: The IEA puts China at about 90% of material recovery capacity. The DoD-MP deal and the Texas magnet campus create domestic pull, and DOE announced $134M for critical-mineral demonstrations in June 2026. Recyclers such as Cyclic Materials and IonicRE are funded and need feed.
revenue_model: Spread between the recycler's price per kg of assayed magnet feed and the yard payout plus pull cost. Optional premium for defense-traceable lots. Small SaaS fee for the identification and price app.
non_obvious_insight: Rare-earth economics fail on tiny magnets (HDDs) but work on a few heavy items. No one publishes a price by motor model, so yards do not know a rotor holds hundreds of grams to kilograms of NdFeB. Price discovery is the missing product, not a new chemistry.
first_30_days: Buy 5 gauss meters. Visit 10 auto shredders and motor shops and measure and photograph 200 units. Build a price sheet by model. Get an offtake LOI from one magnet recycler that needs feed. Pay 3 yards on the first 50 units and publish the results to recruit more.

title: Parametric Cover Against Career-Field Collapse
one_liner: Index-based protection that pays out when hiring in a specific occupation falls past a threshold, sold first to bootcamps, income-share funds and private student lenders whose job-guarantee promises are now correlated bets on entry-level demand.
customer: Bootcamps with job guarantees, ISA funds, private student lenders and university tuition-protection programs. Later, workers via employers and universities as a benefit.
problem: These institutions underwrite outcomes assuming stable entry-level demand. If CS, marketing or analytics hiring drops 30% they all fail together, and no hedge exists. The tail risk is now visible (22-25-year-olds in exposed jobs 19% below trend, junior tech postings down ~35% in major EU countries in 2024).
solution: Phase 1 (about 6 months): publish an Occupation Demand Index (postings, hires, claims mix by occupation and metro) plus stress-test analytics, sold as a subscription to lenders and ISA funds. Phase 2: structure parametric covers through an MGA, fronting carrier and reinsurers, triggered by the index. Phase 3: consumer livelihood cover via employers and universities.
why_now: Occupation-level posting data (e.g. Indeed Hiring Lab) is rich, AI exposure is a new correlated risk, parametric insurance infrastructure has matured, ISA funds and bootcamps are under strain, and event-contract markets are normalised.
revenue_model: Analytics subscriptions ($30-120k a year) first, then premiums and ceding commissions.
non_obvious_insight: Occupational risk has never been hedged because individual triggers create moral hazard. An index solves that for institutions whose portfolio effectively is the occupation, and AI displacement is exactly the correlated tail that reinsurers price.
first_30_days: Build the index from public BLS and posting data and backtest against bootcamp outcome reports. Pitch 10 ISA funds, bootcamps and private lenders a paid $10-25k stress-test pilot.

title: Magnetic Maps for GPS-Denied Drone Navigation
one_liner: A data company that maps low-altitude magnetic anomalies and sells the layers that let cheap drones navigate without GPS.
customer: Drone makers and integrators in Drone Dominance and Navy autonomy programs who need GPS-denied performance, and later defense agencies seeking quantum navigation.
problem: Jamming defeats GPS, and magnetic navigation needs detailed low-altitude field maps. Public datasets are coarse, and hardware teams do not want to become mapping companies. The Navy is asking for quantum navigation and degraded-environment navigation.
solution: Fly survey drones carrying vector magnetometers over test ranges, training areas and border regions, publish tiles through an API, and provide a reference navigation filter that drone makers can integrate. Start with the Gauntlet region and US test ranges.
why_now: Cheap, sensitive magnetometers and onboard compute make magnetic navigation practical for small drones. Fleets of attritable drones can also continuously enrich the map. The Navy calls for quantum and degraded-network navigation (verify map resolution claims).
revenue_model: Per-area annual licences ($20-100K per region), per-tile API access, and custom survey work for programs. Defense SBIR funding for range expansion.
non_obvious_insight: The map, not the sensor, is the moat and it compounds. Every drone that flies with a magnetometer improves the map, so the mapping firm becomes the network owner.
first_30_days: Buy two survey rigs and map one test range and one agricultural area. Publish accuracy results. Offer 3 Gauntlet participants a pilot navigation filter and tile access.

title: Outfall Guardian for Data-Center Construction Sites
one_liner: Continuous outfall monitoring, rapid pathogen testing and auto-generated permit paperwork for contractors building data-center campuses and fabs.
customer: General contractors, owner's representatives and developers building $1B+ data-center and semiconductor campuses. Multi-million-dollar schedule risk gives them a real budget, and the contractor or owner pays.
problem: Cheyenne revoked Meta's discharge permit after a rare bacterium in its wastewater was traced to a construction site, and Ohio scrapped a general permit after more than 7,000 comments. Water quality, not just quantity, is now a siting risk. Contractors treat water as volume and have no biology or continuous-monitoring capability during dewatering, stormwater and hydrostatic testing.
solution: Off-the-shelf multiparameter sensors (turbidity, pH, conductivity, temperature) at each outfall, weekly rapid qPCR pathogen and bacterial testing through a partner lab, automated discharge-monitoring reports and a time-stamped 'permit defense file' that shows compliance before regulators ask. Add a community-facing dashboard.
why_now: Moratoria, permit revocations and public comment fights make regulators and neighbors ask for data. Capex on campuses has exploded, and delay costs are large.
revenue_model: $3-8k/site/month plus per-test lab fees and onboarding fees.
non_obvious_insight: The construction phase is the unmonitored weak link in a water-quality chain everyone else audits. Third-party telemetry works like insurance-grade evidence, and the buyer's motive is schedule protection, not sustainability.
first_30_days: Publish an analysis of the Cheyenne case as top-of-funnel. Contact 10 contractors and owner's reps active in Northern Virginia, Ohio, Texas, Wyoming and Arizona. Pilot at one site with commercial sensors and a contract lab, and offer the first month free in exchange for a case study.

title: Signed Authority Certificates for Buying Agents
one_liner: Companies issue legally strong, machine-verifiable certificates saying which agent may order what, up to what amount, from whom, so suppliers can trust agent-placed orders.
customer: EU industrial distributors and wholesalers that receive purchase orders by email or EDI, and their larger business customers deploying procurement agents. Start with DACH and Benelux distributors.
problem: A supplier gets an order from 'Acme's purchasing agent' and has no way to know it may bind Acme to a EUR 50k purchase. AI makes fake purchase orders and business email compromise cheaper. Consumer-oriented agent-payment mandates (AP2, TAP, Verifiable Intent) do not cover B2B signing authority, and research notes from 2026 say agents do not map cleanly onto EU digital wallet categories.
solution: An authority registry and issuance service. A company's legal representative signs a delegation certificate (qualified electronic signature via eIDAS trust providers, EUDI wallet later) covering agent key, scope (categories or SKUs), per-order and monthly limits, validity and revocation. Suppliers verify by API in under 200 ms and see remaining limit. Integrate with ERP order intake and e-invoicing. The signed record is court-grade evidence in disputes.
why_now: EU member states must offer digital identity wallets by end-2026, financial institutions are expected to accept them by December 2027, and qualified signatures already carry the legal effect of handwritten ones. Agent mandate standards exist but are consumer-centric.
revenue_model: EUR 99-499/month per issuing company, EUR 0.05-0.20 per supplier verification, and enterprise licenses.
non_obvious_insight: Legal effect, not cryptography, is the scarce ingredient in B2B agent commerce. The EU uniquely has an instrument (the qualified signature) that turns a delegation into evidence courts accept, so build where the law already does the hard part.
first_30_days: Integrate with one qualified trust service provider for signing. Interview 20 distributors about agent-placed orders and PO fraud, pilot with 3 distributors and their top buyers on existing order intake, and collect letters of intent.

title: Subsurface Desert Mapping From Free Radar Satellites
one_liner: Use open L-band radar data to map buried channels and structures beneath arid ground for mineral and water explorers.
customer: Junior critical-mineral explorers, uranium and lithium prospectors, groundwater drillers, national geological surveys and arid-region water utilities.
problem: Exploration in deserts costs a fortune per drill hole, targeting is often guesswork, and airborne geophysics is expensive. Explorers need cheaper first-pass targeting.
solution: Combine weekly-repeat NISAR L-band radar (open data), Sentinel-1 and, outside North America and Europe, ESA Biomass P-band to map buried paleo-channels, faults and shallow structure in hyper-arid terrain. Deliver target packages per license block, plus a success-fee option.
why_now: NISAR launched in July 2025 with an open-data policy, and ESA's Biomass P-band radar launched in April 2025. Demand for critical minerals is at a peak. Radar penetration only works in very dry ground, so scope is narrow but valuable.
revenue_model: $20-60k per license block. Success fee or royalty on discoveries. Annual subscriptions for geological surveys.
non_obvious_insight: Seeing beneath sand from orbit sounds like science fiction, and it is now possible with free data. The business is expertise and interpretation, not satellites.
first_30_days: Pick two well-studied arid areas as proof cases and reproduce known buried channels. Show results to 20 junior explorers with licenses in arid regions. Sell the first two block packages at a discount for case studies.

title: Funding Waterfall at the Vet Estimate
one_liner: Front-desk software that routes each vet estimate to the cheapest available funding: insurance advance, charity grant, clinic plan, or credit.
customer: Independent and affordable-care vet clinics as the subscriber. Charitable funds and lenders are paying counterparties.
problem: 85% of vet professionals say clients decline care at estimates of $1,000 or less, and 13% of euthanasias are attributed to inability to pay. Funding sources exist but are fragmented: reimbursement-model insurers pay weeks later, dozens of small charity funds are unknown at the front desk, and mainstream medical credit charges clinics steep fees. New philanthropy has no distribution pipe, so grants like Duffield's are hard to place and audit.
solution: An 'estimate inbox' where the front desk emails or prints the estimate, with no PIMS integration. Within minutes it returns a ranked stack: (1) a 0% claim advance for insured pets secured by the expected reimbursement; (2) pre-screened charity or grant matches; (3) a clinic-carried 0% plan backed by a shared default-guarantee pool; (4) conventional credit. One application, one payout to the clinic in 24-48 hours, with compliance reporting for funders.
why_now: The Duffield Foundation committed $250M over 5 years on Sept 17, 2026 (first grants: 250 x $10K plus $10M multi-year), building on PetSmart Charities' $100M pledge. Neither has pipes for high-volume, low-friction placement. Insurance premiums are up 19.7% against animals up 9%, and clinics are being coached on money conversations. Instant payment rails let clinics be paid the same day.
revenue_model: Clinics pay 1-2% of routed funding or $199 a month. Funders pay about 5% of grant flow as an admin fee, which is cheaper than their own staff. Lenders pay origination fees.
non_obvious_insight: The decline decision is made in a 90-second front-desk moment, and every funding source is built for a different moment. Whoever owns the estimate document owns the routing, and philanthropic money is desperate for a distribution pipe with audit trails.
first_30_days: Sign 15 independent clinics in one metro and run the waterfall as a concierge service with spreadsheets and email. Approach one small pet charity and apply as an infrastructure partner to the Duffield programme. Find one claim-advance lender willing to take insurer-receivable risk on a pilot basis.

title: Operating System For Staff Cooperatives
one_liner: Digitise the exercise-book ledgers of workplace cooperatives, which are the cheapest credit pipe for Nigerian civil servants and teachers, then connect their idle surpluses to each other.
customer: Thrift-and-credit cooperative societies for teachers, nurses, civil servants, police, university staff and market associations. Their executive committees pay for the software. Later, the MFB or bank partner that funds wholesale lending between cooperatives.
problem: Outsiders assume Nigerian salary earners borrow from loan apps or MFBs. In reality a huge share borrow from staff cooperatives at about 10% flat per year, with payroll check-off giving near-zero defaults. But most societies run on Excel, exercise books and a treasurer's WhatsApp. Collapses come from embezzlement, unreconciled employer remittances, and members who cannot see their balances. Some cooperatives sit on idle surplus at 3-8% in a savings account while others in the same city ration loans to a waiting list.
solution: A WhatsApp-first ledger and treasury app: member savings and shares, loan applications with digital guarantors, approval workflows, automated reconciliation of employer check-off remittances against the deduction schedule, monthly member statements, and AGM voting and dividends. AI vision digitises the old exercise books on day one from phone photos. Once ledgers are clean and trusted, add an inter-cooperative wholesale line, routed through a bank or MFB partner, where surplus societies lend to constrained ones at a spread.
why_now: Multimodal AI can now read handwritten ledgers cheaply and reliably, which removes the onboarding barrier that killed earlier software. Tighter FCCPC rules on digital lenders have thinned out predatory apps and pushed members back toward cooperatives. Inflation and salary delays have raised demand for member loans. Open banking and cheaper payout APIs let cooperatives collect and disburse without paper cheques.
revenue_model: SaaS of about N25k-100k per month per cooperative, or N100-200 per member per month. A 0.5-1% spread on inter-cooperative wholesale loans. Fees on embedded products for members (insurance, school-fee financing, phones and gadgets) via the platform.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not capital or customers but trusted records. Once a cooperative's ledger is clean and independent, it becomes a credit-bearing entity and its members can become a distribution channel, which is why the software is a wedge into wholesale lending. The check-off arrangement with the employer is the underwriting moat that no fintech can replicate.
first_30_days: Approach 10 cooperatives through teachers' unions, hospital staff associations and state civil-service networks. Digitise their books free using photo OCR, then start charging from month two. Get an accountant or cooperative-federation officer as a paid advisor for credibility. Track the first reconciliation win, such as finding a missing month of employer remittance, and use it as the case study.

title: Cool-Hours Slot Exchange for Tour Operators
one_liner: Forecast-driven heat re-scheduling for tour operators, plus a marketplace that sells 7am and 8pm venue slots, turning the coolest hours of the day into a priced, allocated resource.
customer: Independent ground-tour operators, destination management companies and cruise shore-excursion desks (10-200 guides) in Athens, Rome, Seville, Marrakech, Petra and Kyoto. The supply side is private venues (wineries, palazzi, small museums, cooking schools) with unused early and late capacity.
problem: Overtourism policy fixates on fees and caps, but the real crush is temporal: coaches, lunch and check-out times funnel everyone into 10:00-15:00, exactly when heat peaks. Operators cancel and refund ad hoc, guides carry heat-illness risk, and there is no record of duty-of-care decisions for insurers under package-travel liability. Meanwhile venues sit empty at dawn and dusk.
solution: Three layers. (1) A scheduler that ingests 5-day heat-stress (WBGT/UTCI) forecasts and the operator's tour book, rebuilds itineraries (dawn starts, indoor midday, evening loops), messages guests in their language and re-checks availability. (2) A time-stamped duty-of-care log (decisions, water and shade stops, guest health flags) exportable to insurers. (3) A slot exchange where venues list early and late timed entries at a premium and operators buy allotments in bulk. Venues get demand data to justify extended hours.
why_now: Summer 2026 Europe saw record heat and a reported provisional death toll near 38,000 (secondary source), pushing operators and regulators toward heat rules. Destinations are moving from fees to allocation: Venice's day-tripper fee reportedly did not cut numbers, while Mount Fuji's hard 4,000/day cap plus fee works. Allocation needs tooling nobody has built. Margins are squeezed by jet-fuel-driven cost increases, so avoiding refunds matters.
revenue_model: EUR 199-499 per month SaaS per operator (tiered by guide count), 4-6% take on slot-exchange GMV, and paid analytics for venues and DMOs ($10-30K per year).
non_obvious_insight: Heat converts overtourism from a space problem into a time problem, and cool hours are the unpriced scarce commodity. They can be allocated like airport slots. Operators are natural demand aggregators, so a small team can win venue supply by promising bulk purchase. The duty-of-care log is what gets insurers interested, because it cuts claim exposure.
first_30_days: Interview 20 Athens and Rome operators about summer 2026 heat-day losses. Build the scheduler as a WhatsApp plus Google Sheets workflow on open forecast data for 5 pilot operators. Get 5 private venues to commit to 08:00 or 19:30 allotments. Demo at WTM London (Nov 2026) and FITUR Madrid (Jan 2027), and convert pilots to paid before the 2027 season.

title: Size-Glide: Reversible Tailoring for GLP-1 Wardrobes
one_liner: Prepaid mail-in take-in tailoring, done with reversible seams, that follows a GLP-1 patient down (and back up) through 3-5 sizes, sold as a retention perk to the telehealth programs that prescribe the drugs.
customer: Two payers. (1) Consumers in months 3-18 of GLP-1 treatment, mostly women 35-60 with a professional wardrobe worth $2-5k. (2) GLP-1 telehealth and employer weight-management programs, who pay a per-member fee because churn is their biggest cost.
problem: Patients drop 2-5 sizes in a year. Buying a new wardrobe at each stage costs $1-3k. Local tailors are slow, inconsistent and expensive, and permanent take-ins ruin a garment when weight comes back. Roughly half of users stop within a year and most regain, so the wardrobe problem repeats in both directions. Programs also lack a tangible, celebratory milestone reward that keeps people enrolled.
solution: A prepaid alteration bag ships to your door. A vetted network of micro-tailors runs a standardized 12-garment menu (waist, hem, darts, sleeves) using reversible methods: basted or removable seams and preserved allowances. Every garment gets a QR tag and a digital 'garment passport' recording each alteration and its size band. Weight milestones trigger reminders ('you are down 15 lb, send the blazers'). A let-out service and a resale or donate-out handoff handle regain and garments that are now too big. Telehealth partners can offer 'your first three take-ins are free' as a milestone reward.
why_now: The Wegovy pill launched in January 2026 and Lilly's oral drug is rolling out this year. GLP-1 households now command roughly $660B in spending power (Numerator, August 2026). Employer coverage and cost pressure are creating start-stop cycles, which makes reversible work the safer product.
revenue_model: Prepaid alteration packs of $250-600 per stage, or a $39-79/month wardrobe plan. B2B2C: $10-25 per member per month from telehealth and employer programs as a retention benefit. Small margin on resale handoffs.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not clothing, it is tailor turnaround and the trust that a garment can come back to its old size. Reversibility is the moat because regain is the norm, not the exception. The best paying customer is the telehealth company's churn budget, not the patient.
first_30_days: Recruit 5 alteration shops in one metro and write a 12-item price menu. Post in r/Zepbound and r/Ozempic communities and local GLP-1 clinic groups to sell 50 prepaid packs. Run a pilot with one small GLP-1 clinic or telehealth startup using free milestone take-ins. Use QR tags and a spreadsheet for the garment passport, and courier pickup for logistics.

title: Idle Brewery Tanks as Biotech Pilot Plants
one_liner: Retrofit closing or underused craft breweries into shared 200 to 2,000 liter fermentation pilot plants for food-ingredient, cosmetic-ingredient and biomaterial startups.
customer: Pre-seed to Series A synthetic-biology and food-tech startups that need samples, regulatory batches and customer trials at pilot scale, plus struggling brewery owners who get rent or revenue share.
problem: Startups can make grams in the lab but face a valley before contract manufacturers will touch them: schedules booked, minimums high, and building their own plant is slow. Pilot-scale fermentation capacity is a widely reported gap. Meanwhile craft brewers are closing: 481 closures against 300 openings in 2025, and 9,344 breweries operating in June 2026, down 1.8% year over year.
solution: A 'bio-foundry co-op'. Lease off-hours tank time from 1 to 3 breweries. Add a portable sterile-air skid, in-place cleaning and sterilization protocols, a single-use inoculum train, and harvest and dewatering equipment (decanter or centrifuge, with drying done through mobile partners). Start with well-characterized yeast (Saccharomyces, Pichia) and other low-risk hosts. Sell fixed-price run packages, with brewer-trained operators supervised by a process scientist.
why_now: Breweries are stranded with stainless tanks, utilities, trade-waste permits and skilled operators, while beer volume keeps shrinking. Food and materials biotech has more strains than pilot capacity. The gap is at 500 to 2,000 liters, not 100,000, and that is exactly brewery scale.
revenue_model: Per-run fees ($8k to $25k), tech-transfer and process-development fees, a rent or revenue share to the brewery, and later a multi-year reserved-capacity subscription for repeat customers.
non_obvious_insight: The moat isn't the tank, it's the permitting: zoning, industrial wastewater discharge capacity for high-BOD effluent, food-grade utilities and a building already approved for fermentation take biotech companies years to secure. Breweries have all of it. Brewers are also the biggest pool of people who instinctively know how to keep yeast at scale contamination-free.
first_30_days: Sign a letter of intent with one distressed brewery on an off-hours share. Recruit 3 startups from synbio and food-tech directories and sell a paid $5k to $10k feasibility run at 200 liters. Prepare a biosafety plan and speak to the local wastewater authority early. Line up a part-time process scientist.

title: Guardrail Gateway for Law-Firm AI Agents
one_liner: A policy proxy between AI agents and practice-management, billing and trust-accounting systems that enforces ethics rules (trust funds, conflicts, confidentiality) and logs every action for the bar and the insurer.
customer: Solo and small firms (5 or fewer attorneys), the exact segment adopting MCP connectors. Distribution partners are practice-management vendors and malpractice carriers that want to underwrite agent use.
problem: 8am's MyCase MCP connector exposes 73 actions across cases, billing and intake, and 60+ firms adopted it in month one. An agent that can write to billing and trust ledgers can commingle funds, send a privileged detail to the wrong client or email a client without review. Those are disciplinary and malpractice events that no hallucination checker prevents, and solo lawyers have no IT staff, policy or audit trail.
solution: An MCP gateway between Claude, ChatGPT or a 'Firm Agent' and Clio, MyCase and LawPay. Rules block any write touching the trust account without attorney approval by SMS, enforce ethical walls between matters, redact privileged content going to non-approved models, hold outbound client communications for review and rate-limit actions. Every call goes into a tamper-evident log, and a monthly 'agent audit' PDF answers the insurer questionnaire.
why_now: 8am launched its MCP integration in Sep 2026 and says nearly all of its new Firm Agent features already work via MCP, so law-practice data is flowing to third-party agents for the first time. ABA Formal Opinion 512 (2024) on generative-AI ethics gives the duties a written source (background, verify).
revenue_model: $79-199/firm/month, carrier-sponsored programs at $10-20 per insured firm per month, and white-label licensing to practice-management vendors.
non_obvious_insight: The risk from agents is authority (moving money and information), not wrong words. Legal ethics rules are crisp about authority (trust accounting, confidentiality, conflicts), so they compile into policy, unlike 'accuracy'. Distribution will run through practice-management marketplaces, not law-firm websites.
first_30_days: Build the gateway for one platform (Clio or MyCase MCP) with six rules. Recruit 10 small firms through user groups and run it free as a 30-day 'agent audit' that shows near-misses, then convert at $99/month. Take the audit output to two state-bar-affiliated malpractice carriers.

title: Independent Conformance Bench for CMS-0057-F APIs
one_liner: A testing-and-attestation service that runs the open-source Inferno and Da Vinci test kits against a health plan's real FHIR APIs and produces the evidence pack its compliance officer needs before January 2027.
customer: Small and mid-size Medicaid managed-care plans, regional Medicare Advantage plans, CHIP managed-care entities, TPAs and the small payer-IT vendors serving them. Buyer is the compliance officer or CIO who signed a vendor contract and can't verify it.
problem: CMS-0057-F requires four FHIR APIs (Patient Access, Provider Access, Payer-to-Payer, Prior Authorization) by 1 Jan 2027, and the 72-hour and 7-day decision timelines have applied since Jan 2026. Plans bought vendor stacks and hear 'we're compliant,' but the plan carries the liability. CMS points at ONC's Inferno tooling, yet almost no one independent runs it against the plan's production-like environment and writes the attestation.
solution: A managed test bench: Inferno with the Da Vinci PAS/CRD/DTR and CARIN test kits, Synthea synthetic members mapped to the plan's data model, latency and load tests aligned to the decision-time metrics, and SMART/OAuth security checks. Deliverables are a pass/fail matrix, remediation tickets for the vendor, an executive attestation binder, and quarterly regression runs as vendors ship updates.
why_now: Guidance is that plans commit to a stack by Q3 2026 to leave time for testing, so Q4 2026 is the test window. It is late September. The rule is fixed, the open-source test kits exist, and the buyers' vendors have a conflict of interest in grading themselves.
revenue_model: Fixed-fee readiness assessment of USD 15-40k. Quarterly regression subscription of USD 3-8k per month. Vendor-side 'independently tested' certification fee. Optional remediation project work.
non_obvious_insight: The buyer isn't engineering; it's a compliance officer who needs independent evidence to hold a vendor to account. Inferno has huge adoption among developers but has never been packaged as an auditor's deliverable. Independence, not tooling, is the product.
first_30_days: Spin up a hosted Inferno plus Synthea environment. Publish a free 'CMS-0057-F self-test cheat sheet.' Approach 10 Medicaid MCO compliance officers through state Medicaid association events and LinkedIn. Sell three pilot assessments at about USD 10k to build case studies before year-end. Partner with FHIR consultancies that lack independent status.

title: Lot-Level Verification for Generic Semaglutide Importers
one_liner: A shared-API lineage database plus independent identity and impurity testing for distributors and pharmacy chains buying the flood of post-patent generic semaglutide.
customer: Distributors, pharmacy chains, hospital groups and telehealth clinics in India, Canada, Brazil and the 75+ markets Indian exporters like Hetero now target, and payers or regulators who need lot-level evidence.
problem: Semaglutide patents lapsed in Canada (Jan 2026), India and Brazil (Mar 2026), and 40+ Indian companies launched brands within weeks. By July, Dr. Reddy's halted supply through at least late October over an API impurity, and Torrent recalled Semalix batches after Dr. Reddy's notice because it uses the same API. Buyers can't see which brands share which API source, and fake pens circulate.
solution: Build an API-lineage graph from customs and shipping records, regulatory notices, recalls and public dossiers, mapping each brand and batch to its API manufacturer, and alert subscribers when any brand in the shared-API cluster has an event. Pair this with fast lot testing (LC-MS peptide identity and purity, impurity profile) through accredited partner labs in India, the UAE and Brazil, returning a signed 'verified lot' certificate with QR lookup. Start with a free public recall-radar page and newsletter to collect buyers.
why_now: Generics launched in March-July 2026 across three large markets at once (India prices as low as Rs 1,500 a month), regulators are stretched, and the first recalls and counterfeit guidance are already published. Tirzepatide and US semaglutide remain patented, so the gray market will keep growing alongside the legitimate one.
revenue_model: $250-$600 per verified lot, $500-$2,000 a month for lineage alerts and API access, and custom supplier audits for hospital groups and exporters.
non_obvious_insight: Forty-plus brands is not forty-plus independent risks: a handful of API sources means one impurity event propagates across supposedly competing brands, and no buyer-side tool maps that. Evidence: BusinessLine's headline 'DRL's semaglutide supply hits a stumbling block, affects other companies too' and Economic Times' Torrent recall after Dr. Reddy's notice (Jul 9, 2026) via Google News (https://news.google.com/rss/search?q=Torrent+Semalix+recall+Dr+Reddy%27s+API+semaglutide+Canada); Fierce Pharma on the pause (https://www.fiercepharma.com/manufacturing/dr-reddys-presses-pause-generic-semaglutide-supply-after-flagging-api-issue). India Today: 'Quality concerns hit cheap Ozempic copies in India within months'. NDTV, Mar 30, 2026: 'How To Spot Fakes'. Hetero: 1.5M pens, 75+ markets (Medical Dialogues Apr 16, 2026). Patent-expiry dates and 40-50 brands: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semaglutide.
first_30_days: Days 1-7: assemble a public database of every Indian semaglutide brand, the marketing-authorization holder, contract manufacturer and any disclosed API source, and ship the recall-radar page. Days 7-20: sign a testing-lab partner in India or the UAE on a wholesale per-lot price, and run 20 lots bought retail as a published 'state of the market' report. Days 20-30: pitch 25 importers, pharmacy chains and telehealth clinics with a free lineage check plus a $400 lot test, and aim for 5 paid tests.

title: Hardware-Origin Audits for Drones and Robots
one_liner: Teardown-level bill-of-materials and firmware audits that prove what is really inside a 'US-made' drone or robot, sold to small makers, to the public-safety and utility buyers who must prove compliance, and to insurers.
customer: US drone and robot makers with 5-100 employees selling to public safety, utilities, agriculture and federally funded programs. Buyers: county, city and state procurement offices and grant recipients. Insurers and lenders who need 'no covered components' assurance.
problem: The FCC barred new DJI and Autel models in Dec 2025, US drone tariffs took effect in Sep 2026 with component tariffs in 2027, and China's export controls cover motors, batteries, radios and sensors. Buyers must show they bought compliant gear, but suppliers self-declare, rebrand and reroute. Procurement staff cannot inspect a flight controller. After the IEEPA tariff-refund saga, customs origin claims will draw scrutiny. Unitree G1 at about $16k tempts robot buyers into the same problem.
solution: An auditor plus registry. Teardown-level BOM verification (identify chips and modules, firmware and network-callback tests for covered-vendor endpoints, cross-check of supplier declarations and customs documents). It produces a signed origin and compliance dossier per model and lot. A public registry lets procurement staff query a model against state and federal restrictions.
why_now: The FCC action, tariffs and Chinese export controls all landed between Dec 2025 and Sep 2026. Domestic supply is emerging (Amprius won a $75M award for 500 Wh/kg cells), and dozens of new entrants all claim 'American-made'. A number of state laws also restrict agencies from buying Chinese drones (specifics to verify).
revenue_model: $8k-$30k per product audit for makers. $1k-$3k per re-certification on a BOM change. $2k-$5k/yr buyer-side registry subscription for agencies. Lot-level spot-check fees. Referral fees from insurers.
non_obvious_insight: When a ban creates a market, the scarce asset is belief in compliance, not the compliant product. The audit fee is a tax on every new entrant, and buyers fear being embarrassed by an audit finding. Inputs are cheap (a bench, a spectrum analyzer, firmware tooling) and one engineer can produce the first audits. The same dossier doubles as customs-origin evidence.
first_30_days: With maker consent (or from public teardowns), audit 5 currently marketed 'American-made' drones and publish the methodology. Offer three small US makers a $5k pre-audit with a money-back guarantee. Sell 3 full audits at $10k-$15k. Pitch a state public-safety procurement association on the registry.

title: Convert Legacy RPA Bots Using Their Own Logs
one_liner: Use years of bot execution logs as free ground-truth tests to convert brittle RPA bots into monitored agents at a fixed price per bot.
customer: Mid-market companies (500-10,000 employees) with 20-300 UiPath, Blue Prism or Power Automate bots in finance ops, claims and HR, plus RPA consultancies as a channel.
problem: Vendor and consultancy estimates put RPA upkeep at several times license cost, and UI changes break bots constantly. Leaders want agents but fear regression, and migration advice is generic ('retire the brittle ones first'). RPA vendors are pivoting to agentic pitches themselves, which increases pressure without giving a safe method.
solution: Ingest bot definitions and run logs, replay historical inputs to a candidate agent, and differentially test its outputs against the bot's recorded outputs. Cut over each bot when parity passes a threshold, keep the old bot in shadow for 30 days, monitor for drift, and price per bot converted plus a run-and-monitor fee.
why_now: Computer-use agents can operate UIs reliably enough to compete with scripted bots, and RPA vendors are moving to orchestration. Budgets are earmarked because maintenance costs are visible.
revenue_model: $2-$6k per bot conversion plus $200-$500/month per bot run and monitoring, with revenue share for consultancy partners.
non_obvious_insight: The hard part of migrating automations is knowing the new one is right. Legacy bots have already produced years of labeled input-output pairs for free, which turns migration into differential testing.
first_30_days: Find 10 mid-market RPA shops and ask each for 5 brittle bots. Convert 5 bots across 2 customers in shadow mode, show parity, and sign a fixed-fee conversion for the next 20.

title: GLP-1 Alcohol Protocols Inside Sober-Living Homes
one_liner: A turnkey semaglutide-for-alcohol-use-disorder protocol delivered through recovery residences, which supply the daily accountability, testing and peer community that telehealth prescribing lacks.
customer: Sober-living and recovery-residence operators and intensive-outpatient centers, who pass the cost into resident fees of $600-2,500 a month that are usually paid by families.
problem: Very few people with alcohol use disorder get any medication, and a Lancet RCT (May 2026, n=108) showed semaglutide cut heavy drinking days with an NNT of 4.3 versus 7+ for approved drugs. GLP-1 prescribing for it is off-label and sold as DTC telehealth to isolated individuals. Recovery houses have residents, house managers and drug testing, but no medical capability. Operators bleed occupancy and reputation on relapse evictions, and GLP-1 use in liver-compromised drinkers carries real malnutrition, muscle-loss and GI risks that need monitoring.
solution: A partner addiction-medicine physician or telehealth prescriber panel screens and consents residents, using contraindication checks and baseline labs. House managers get training and a daily check-in script (dose day, intake, nausea, cravings). A dietitian sets minimum protein and calorie floors. Weekly peer-recovery groups link medication, craving and community, with a tapering and aftercare plan at discharge. The house sees 30/60/90-day retention and abstinence data.
why_now: The 2026 Lancet RCT and $149-299 cash prices for branded GLP-1s make the drug affordable. Compounded supply is closing, which pushes demand toward branded, clinician-supervised use. Many states are certifying recovery residences, and Medicaid cuts in 2027 make private-pay operators look for outcomes-based differentiation.
revenue_model: $120-200 per resident per month from operators (passed through in rent), plus clinician-visit billing or revenue share with the prescriber, and an aftercare subscription for graduates.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce input for alcohol-use-disorder pharmacotherapy is adherence and monitoring, not the prescription. Telehealth sells scripts to lonely individuals, while sober-living houses already have people living together with daily check-ins and testing. The house is the missing delivery infrastructure, and GLP-1 gives it the first credible craving-reduction drug to offer.
first_30_days: Sign one addiction-medicine physician and three operators in one metro (Florida, Texas or California). Enroll about 20 consenting residents with written informed consent, and track 30/60/90-day retention and abstinence days versus the houses' baselines. Use the data to sign the next 10 houses. Get a healthcare attorney's review of the off-label and consent framework before the first dose.

title: Community Radio as a Paid Knowledge API
one_liner: Turn African community-radio call-in shows into a live, district-level, per-call-priced local-truth feed that farm agents and lenders pay for, with stations keeping most of the revenue.
customer: Agri-input distributors, crop insurers, agri-lenders and farmer-facing AI agents (FarmerChat-style services) in East Africa. Community radio stations in Uganda and Kenya are the supply side and get 70% of revenue.
problem: Western models 'fail spectacularly' on African crops, and satellites cannot see this week's pest outbreak, local planting window or market price. Community radio is where farmers self-report and where trusted extension voices answer, but its ad revenue is collapsing. Bots do not click ads, so stations earn nothing when agents consume their knowledge.
solution: Transcribe and structure weekly call-in shows (Luganda, Swahili, Hausa and others) into dated, sourced, district-level signals such as pest reports, price quotes and planting advice, with provenance and consent. Expose them as an MCP or HTTP endpoint with per-call micropayments via x402 or MPP. Add a paid 'ask the station' tier where an agent's question is read on air and the answer captured. Stations receive rev-share via mobile money.
why_now: Small ASR models (300M-1.7B parameters) now handle local languages, and AethexAI already trains on radio audio. FarmerChat has answered 8M+ questions, which proves demand. Machine-payment protocols make micro-charging per call possible, and Cloudflare's pay-per-crawl is training content owners to charge bots.
revenue_model: Per-call fees for agents ($0.005-0.05), district-level monthly subscriptions ($200-600) for lenders and insurers, and premium on-air Q&A. Platform keeps 30% and stations get 70%.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce asset is not a language training set, which is a commodity. It is fresh local ground truth with a trusted human voice behind it, delivered as a live feed rather than an archive. Radio stations are the last network where farmers report in their own words. Content owners who cannot win the ad economy can win the agent-query economy.
first_30_days: Sign 3-5 stations in Uganda and Kenya with a simple rev-share and consent agreement. Record and transcribe two weeks of shows with a fine-tuned open ASR model. Publish a weekly district JSON feed. Sell the first two district subscriptions to an agri-lender or seed distributor at $300-500 a month.

title: Impersonation Firewall at the Distributor Gate
one_liner: A KYC-style API that distributors call before publishing a release under an existing artist name, so one upstream check protects every streaming service at once.
customer: Mid-size self-serve music distributors and label-service companies, which carry the upload volume, the DSP penalties and the legal heat from labels. Estates and small catalogs benefit downstream.
problem: Everyone treats DSP-side approval as the fix, such as Spotify's Artist Profile Protection beta (Mar 24, 2026) and its verified badges (Apr 30). But impersonation enters through distributors, which sit upstream of every DSP. The brief cites Sony's 135,000+ removal requests, and AI tracks were pushed onto pages of Jeff Tweedy, Father John Misty and the late Blaze Foley in Aug 2025. Spotify's protection only helps artists who opt in, on one service.
solution: An API that scores each new release in seconds. It checks (1) name and identifier collisions against existing artist pages on public DSP APIs, (2) proof of control over the claimed identity through handle-linking challenges and a short liveness video for unknown names, and (3) audio-embedding similarity between the new master and the claimed artist's catalog. Suspicious releases go to a human review queue with an evidence pack. It returns allow, hold or reject, and every decision is logged.
why_now: Platform policing arrived (Spotify beta, TIDAL, Bandcamp) but only at the shelf, not the door. Deezer reports AI above 50% of uploads, so distributors face rising takedown and fine volume. AI-powered impersonation is now cheap.
revenue_model: $0.10-0.40 per release check with a $1-3k/month minimum, plus review-queue seats and a premium tier for auto-holding high-risk releases.
non_obvious_insight: The platforms sell AI tools themselves and each protects only its own pages. The distributor is the only place where cost, liability and the payout relationship line up, and a KYC check there is cheap compared with cleanup after upload.
first_30_days: Build a prototype on public Spotify, Deezer and Apple search APIs plus open audio embeddings. Back-test it on the documented impersonation cases. Offer 10 mid-size distributors a free retro-audit of their last 90 days of releases, and convert one or two into a paid pilot.

title: Closing-Risk Radar for New-Construction Loan Officers
one_liner: Forecasts which locked new-build closings will miss their rate-lock window, using permit and inspection data plus builder history, so loan officers extend cheaply or re-price before the buyer walks.
customer: New-construction loan officers and mortgage teams (builder-preferred lenders, community banks), title companies, and small builders' sales managers.
problem: 80-90% of new-home sales need rate buydowns, and completions fell 27.1% as crews vanish, foundations sit idle and electricians are delayed up to 2 months. Closing dates slip, locks expire and buydown funding is stranded. A West Virginia builder is at risk of losing about 40 closings. Nobody forecasts construction slippage, only rates.
solution: For each locked loan, ingest the address and pull permit and inspection status from municipal portals, add the builder's stage photos or one-question SMS replies, and output a slip probability and the cheapest date to extend. Add a monthly builder reliability scorecard for lender risk and builder-relations teams.
why_now: Buydown-dependent sales, mortgage rates near 7%, falling completions and forecast 2027 starts down 2-4% mean lock-expiry losses will climb. LLM-based extraction from messy municipal portals is now cheap.
revenue_model: $25-50 per monitored loan or $400-800 per month per loan officer. Enterprise scorecards for lender risk teams.
non_obvious_insight: Loan officers care about the construction calendar as much as the rate curve, and they have direct fee income at stake when a lock lapses, unlike builders who learn late. Public inspection sequence is a surprisingly strong predictor of slip, and the reliability scorecard is a byproduct with its own buyer.
first_30_days: Sell to five new-construction loan officers in Texas and the Southeast. Each shares 20-40 pending closings. Build the forecast manually in spreadsheets from portals and show five saves in 30 days.

title: Loss Draft Desk for Storm Contractors
one_liner: Software and concierge service that gets contractors and homeowners through the mortgage servicer's loss-draft process, then advances cash against approved draws.
customer: Storm-restoration general contractors, roofers and owner-builders working on mortgage-encumbered repairs and rebuilds, starting with the Palisades and Eaton rebuild wave and Gulf Coast stragglers. Later, homeowners and the servicers' own vendor teams.
problem: The carrier pays, but the money is not free: the check names the mortgagee, and the servicer's loss-draft department decides whether to release it in one lump sum or in staged draws tied to inspections. Each servicer has its own packet (contractor W-9, license, signed contract, lien waivers, before/after photos, inspection scheduling) and its own cadence. Contractors carry 60-120 days of working capital risk, homeowners cannot start work, and adjusters take the blame for a delay that comes after the estimate is done.
solution: A draw-management platform: it reads the carrier's payment letter and the servicer's requirements, auto-builds and submits the servicer-specific packet, schedules and preps for inspections (checklist plus timestamped photo capture), chases the servicer, and shows the contractor and homeowner a live 'money timeline.' Phase two adds a draw advance: after the servicer approves a draw schedule, the platform advances 80-90% of the next draw in days, underwritten on proprietary servicer-by-servicer release data.
why_now: Florida's AOB ban (for policies since 2023) means contractors cannot be paid directly by carriers, so they must wait on homeowners and servicers. The LA fire rebuild in 2026-27 involves thousands of large, mortgage-encumbered claims and long draw schedules. Materials costs remain volatile, which squeezes contractor cash. Regulatory rules and GSE guidelines push servicers to release funds promptly after approving a repair plan but leave the mechanics unstandardized, creating a compliance-flavored process that software can systematize.
revenue_model: Flat $295-$495 per job, or 0.5-1% of funds released. Draw advances at 2-3% of advance amount plus a 30-60 day fee, funded by a warehouse credit line. Later, per-file fees from servicers who want clean packets and fewer complaint escalations.
non_obvious_insight: The real payment terms in disaster repair are the servicer's draw curve, not the insurance company's payment speed, and nobody publishes it. Whoever logs, servicer by servicer, days-to-first-draw, inspection pass rates and packet rejection reasons owns the underwriting data for the only safe lending against insurance proceeds.
first_30_days: Sign up 5 mid-size LA fire rebuild contractors and 5 Gulf Coast roofers and offer to run their next 3 jobs through the loss-draft process as a done-for-you service at $295 per job. Log every servicer requirement in a shared spreadsheet, then turn it into a rules engine. Interview 3 former loss-draft department employees for packet-rejection patterns. Start collecting draw-timeline data, which becomes the moat and the basis for a later advance product.

title: Visitor-Levy Back Office for Councils
one_liner: White-label registration, returns, audit and enforcement software plus a service desk that lets local councils run a new tourist levy without building it.
customer: Local authorities that have just gained the power to levy visitors: Scottish councils, Welsh councils, and Spanish, Balearic and other European municipalities.
problem: Levies are proliferating (Edinburgh in 2026, Glasgow from Jan 2027, Welsh councils from 2027, Balearics and Catalonia rising, Chicago at 19% hotel tax). Each council must register providers, collect returns, audit and chase non-payers, and most have neither software nor staff. Small B&Bs and self-caterers file badly and disputes pile up.
solution: A packaged portal for provider registration and returns, with support for per-night and percentage levies, exemptions, OTA-collected amounts and platform data feeds. It includes automated reminders, audit sampling, a provider help desk and a statutory report pack, configured per council within weeks.
why_now: New statutory levies start across the UK through 2026-27, and EU short-term rental rules require platforms to share host data with authorities from May 2026. That data can be matched against levy returns. Councils' levy revenue lets them fund administration.
revenue_model: GBP 20-60K per council per year, or a share of collected levy, plus per-return service fees for the help desk.
non_obvious_insight: Levies fail on administration rather than on rate-setting. Every council needs the same back office at the same moment, and levy revenue pays for it, so the customer has a budget line before it has a system.
first_30_days: Talk to 10 councils and the Welsh and Scottish local-government bodies. Offer a fixed-fee pilot of a provider portal and returns form for one small council. Build it from a form tool and a database first, then harden.

title: Human Viva Examiners for AI-Wary Universities
one_liner: A per-student oral-defense service where trained examiners in Nairobi, Manila and Chennai run 12-minute recorded vivas on submitted essays and code, giving US professors human-verified authorship evidence for about $10 a student.
customer: Writing-program directors, department chairs and online-degree program managers at US community colleges and mid-size universities (intro composition, intro CS, gateway business courses). Individual adjuncts with discretionary budgets are the first buyers. Admissions offices reviewing flagged essays come second.
problem: Harvard data from Sept 2026: 89% of professors received suspected AI work, 67% say AI hurts their courses, and only 12% referred cases to the honor council. Detectors are unreliable and biased against non-native writers. Nobody has the time or the standing to test an accusation, and a professor cannot personally hold 60 oral exams per section.
solution: The instructor uploads submissions and a rubric. The platform drafts 4-6 questions specific to each student's own paper. AI writes the questions but never judges. A vetted examiner in a matching time zone runs a 12-minute live video viva, scores it against the rubric, and marks the student as able or unable to explain their own work. The instructor gets a one-page evidence summary and the recording within 48 hours. Examiners are ex-teachers and graduate students who pass a 6-hour certification, and 10% of vivas are double-scored for QA. Students consent through the syllabus, and the institution signs a FERPA school-official agreement.
why_now: Faculty AI distress peaked in Sept 2026. NYC and LAUSD paused classroom AI for 2026-27, so 'human-verified' is now politically favored over AI-judging-AI. Proctored math accuracy has fallen from about 80% to about 60% while unsupervised work looks better. Meanwhile English-fluent graduates in Kenya, the Philippines and India face a shrinking entry-level BPO ladder, so a large trainable labor pool is available at $15/hour.
revenue_model: $9-14 per viva billed to the department, with examiners paid about $4-5 per viva (roughly $15/hour), for a gross margin near 55%. Departments can buy an annual site licence of $3-10k. An appeal viva is a $25 add-on.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is not detection, it is credible human attention. Detectors create accusations nobody can test, while a viva turns an accusation into an assessment: if the student can defend the paper, they learned it, however they drafted it. The only way to supply cheap, trusted, trained human minutes at scale is emerging-market labor, and the only buyers who will pay are institutions that just lost faith in remote work.
first_30_days: Recruit and train 15 examiners through two teacher-training colleges or alumni groups in Kenya and the Philippines. Offer three community-college composition instructors a free 30-student pilot and record what share of students cannot explain their own paper. Charge $300 for the next batch, and reach instructors through adjunct communities and online-program managers. Run it on Zoom, a calendar tool and Airtable, with no custom platform until 10 paying sections exist.

title: Play Yards: Phone-Free Adventure Clubs for Tweens
one_liner: Membership 'junk playground' clubs staffed by trained playworkers for ages 9-14 (tools, timber, fire pits, no phones, no lessons), launched first in four-day-school-week districts where Friday is a childcare hole.
customer: Parents of 9-14-year-olds paying $150-250/month for after-school access or $45-60 per full Friday, plus landlords with vacant retail or barns. Some state child-care subsidies and school-choice funds may help later.
problem: Schools are banning phones and governments are restricting youth social media, but kids have nowhere to go for unstructured, semi-supervised time with peers. Structured enrichment (coding camps, leagues) is oversupplied, while true adventure playgrounds are rare, nonprofit and mostly for younger children.
solution: A leased warehouse, church hall or barn plus a yard, stocked with loose parts, real tools and a fire pit, with a 1:12 playworker-to-child ratio. Ship an insurer-approved risk-benefit policy, playworker training, a phone-locker rule and flexible memberships. Anchor demand with full-day Fridays in four-day-week districts, then add weekday afternoons and holiday camps.
why_now: More than 2,100 public schools in 26 states now run four-day weeks and the number is growing, mostly in rural districts with few child-care options. At the same time school phone bans and the 'anxious generation' movement have made parents ask for offline peer time.
revenue_model: Monthly memberships, per-day Friday fees (about $50 x 35-40 Fridays is roughly $2,000 per child per year), birthday parties, holiday camps, and later franchise or license fees.
non_obvious_insight: The scarce good is not activities, it is unsupervised-feeling time with peers, and what makes it sellable is liability engineering: an insurance-approved risk policy and playwork training that let a for-profit offer what municipalities avoid. Four-day weeks give a ready anchor customer (working parents with an empty Friday) that funds the more interesting weekday model.
first_30_days: Choose a four-day-week district with a supportive superintendent and rent a church hall or barn for about $1k/month. Hire two playworkers, secure a youth-program insurance policy, and pre-sell 25 Friday memberships through school newsletters and Facebook groups. Run four pilot Fridays, gather parent and kid feedback, then add after-school hours.
